sources.title: Official CV: education, trade union work and government career
sources.findings: Read official CV: November 19, 1977 Aalborg birth, administration/social-studies bachelor 2007, African-studies master 2009, LO youth consultant 2000–2001, MP since 2001, parliamentary deputy chair 2005–2011, ministerial roles, party leader since 2015 and prime minister since 2019. Degrees postdate first election. Do not turn a master into a PhD or calculate her November 19 birthday as already reached at the November 18 cutoff.

sources.title: Mette Frederiksen: parliamentary mandates and exact ministerial dates
sources.findings: Read Folketing biography and detailed mandate/education sections. November 20, 2001 first Copenhagen County mandate, November 13, 2007 constituency change and June 5, 2019 North Jutland representation; October 3, 2011 employment ministry, October 10, 2014 justice ministry, June 28, 2015 end; June 27, 2019 premiership. Current national legislature is not the European Parliament. No claim that mandate seniority has no leave interruptions.

sources.title: Historical biography: party leadership, 2019 government and policy controversies
sources.findings: Read Lex historical biography on June 28, 2015 unopposed party succession, June 27, 2019 single-party minority cabinet, welfare/immigration strategy and criticism, pandemic and mink inquiry. Support-party parliamentary agreement is not cabinet membership. Its historical account is not used as a complete current-government description; updated official and IPU records establish 2026 changes.

sources.title: Frederiksen II: 15 December 2022 to 3 June 2026, S–V–M coalition
sources.findings: Read official Frederiksen II cabinet register: December 15, 2022–June 3, 2026, Social Democrats, Venstre and Moderates. Subsequent personnel reshuffles are not new premierships or general elections. Earlier December coalition negotiations differ from formal cabinet start; the old composition is not carried into the third government.

sources.title: Frederiksen III government formation, 3 June 2026
sources.findings: Read June 3, 2026 announcement that Frederiksen forms her third government and its minister list. The scheduled royal presentation time alone is not proof of attendance, so formal composition and appointment are cross-checked against the royal resolution, IPU account and Commons Library completed-appointment report.

sources.title: Royal resolution on the new ministry, 3 June 2026
sources.findings: Read selected operative portions of the June 3 royal-resolution PDF, including the reference to March 25 resignation, continuation of Frederiksen as prime minister, ministry reallocations and dated ending. No claim to have authenticated signatures from pixels or exhaustively audited every portfolio. Official resignation/caretaker period and new cabinet formation are not a change of person as prime minister.

sources.title: Denmark’s 24 March 2026 election and June government formation
sources.findings: Read IPU election summary: March 24, 2026 vote, Social Democrats 50 to 38 seats, June 1 agreement announcement, June 3 government taking office. Coalition changed from S–V–M to S–SF–M–RV and is a minority. SF’s English Green Left name corresponds to Socialist People’s Party; RV is Social Liberal, distinct from Venstre. No invented direct presidential election or parliamentary majority.

sources.title: Denmark: 2026 election and new coalition government, 12 June 2026
sources.findings: Read Commons Library June 12, 2026 briefing landing page and substantive summary confirming March election and June 3 formal appointment of a third minority government. Full downloadable report not reviewed. Earlier polls and predicted election effects are not recorded as final outcomes.

sources.title: Climate bill L 117: adopted 18 June 2020, legal target and cross-party vote
sources.findings: Read Folketing L117 history, summary and vote: June 18, 2020 adoption, Act 965 dated June 26, 70% greenhouse-gas reduction target by 2030 versus 1990, cross-party support and planning duties. The then-2050 neutrality target is historical and omitted rather than assumed current after subsequent changes. Statutory goals are not verified completed reductions or legislation personally enacted by the prime minister.

sources.publisher: Folketinget — Committee on the Standing Orders
sources.title: Report no. 24 on Mink Commission findings, 8 July 2022
sources.findings: Read selected substantive sections of Committee on Standing Orders report no.24, dated July 8, 2022, especially majority assessment paragraphs on November 3 decision process/November 4 announcement, serious political criticism, lack of legal authority and no grounds found by the majority for impeachment charges. It accepted she lacked relevant knowledge/intent; this is not a criminal court’s blanket acquittal. No full multi-volume Mink Commission file review claimed.

sources.title: Political reprimand and no impeachment over mink cull, 5 July 2022
sources.findings: Read Euronews July 5, 2022 completed reprimand account with AFP sourcing. Corroborates political criticism, missing authority for blanket cull and no impeachment; she acknowledged mistakes and denied prior knowledge of the legal gap. Distinguish July 5 committee action, July 8 report date and June 30 commission report. No assumption all mink were actually killed on November 4.

sources.title: Frederiksen and Zelenskyy meet Copenhagen students, 10 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Ukraine presidency’s November 10, 2026 completed Copenhagen student-meeting report and Frederiksen’s attributed remarks. It confirms her participation and support position. November 17 global latest-news entries are not this event’s date. Aid promises, negotiations and future meetings are not completed deliveries or peace; no video/audio inspection claimed.

sources.title: Public preview: Frederiksen’s Dublin remarks on 12 November, published 13 November 2026
sources.findings: Read public Ritzau/Copenhagen Post preview dated November 13, 2026, explicitly placing remarks and Dublin arrival on Thursday November 12. Full article is subscriber-only and was not accessed. It supports actual recent appearance, not completion of a proposed non-EU return centre or the forecast following-week announcement.
